plan.change: Make required static checks path-applicable so non-applicable checks are explicit N/A instead of fake PASS or permanent failure.
expectedChanges: Represent required static checks in the Risk Policy with explicit path applicability metadata.
Treat a required static check as N/A when none of the changed paths for that risk profile match its applicability, rather than requiring a declaration or treating the check as PASS.
Keep node-syntax required for Change OS changes that include .js, .cjs, or .mjs files.
Keep change-operations-regression required for every Change OS change.
Add regression tests for workflow/docs-only Change OS changes, JavaScript Change OS changes, and missing applicable node-syntax declarations.
Document that static-check applicability is derived from the trusted Risk Policy before execution evidence is evaluated.
hqDecisions: Non-applicable static checks must be represented as N/A, never PASS.
Applicability belongs to the trusted Risk Policy that derives required checks from changed paths.
This package fixes only the applicability contract needed by C3-2 and does not add the trusted static registry/executor.
plan.manualCheckExemptionReason: Change OS contract repair verified by trusted CI, regression tests, and PR review; authenticated human attestation is out of scope.
plan.rollback: Revert this staging Change OS package if static-check applicability weakens an applicable requirement or breaks trusted gates.
unverified: C3-2 remains incomplete until the separate trusted registry/executor package is implemented after this prerequisite is merged.
plan.problem: The current Change OS risk profile requires node-syntax for every Change OS path, including workflow and documentation-only changes where there is no JavaScript to check. C3-2 cannot truthfully mark a non-executed syntax check PASS, while treating no applicable JavaScript as failure would make valid non-JavaScript Change OS changes unmergeable.
plan.currentContract: tools/change-risk-policy.cjs stores unconditional requiredStaticChecks arrays per profile, and tools/change-risk-check.cjs requires every listed ID to appear in Plan.staticChecks.
plan.whyExistingIsInsufficient: Static check names were previously declarative only, so applicability was not observable. Trusted execution makes the missing applicability contract blocking.
plan.design: Extend each risk profile's required static-check entries with trusted path applicability metadata. The Risk Check derives applicable paths per check. If none match, it emits N/A risk.static-check-not-applicable and does not require the Plan to declare that check. If any match, the existing declaration requirement remains mandatory. change-operations-regression uses always applicability; node-syntax uses JavaScript extensions .js/.cjs/.mjs.
alternativesRejected: Treat no applicable JavaScript as node-syntax PASS; that would label an unexecuted check PASS.
Keep node-syntax unconditionally required and fail workflow/docs-only Change OS changes; that would create a permanent false blocker.
Move applicability into the future C3-2 executor only; Risk Gate would still require a non-applicable check before execution.
Remove node-syntax from the Change OS risk profile entirely; JavaScript Change OS changes would lose an existing safety requirement.
plan.migration: No Plan Lock or historical record is rewritten. Future Risk Gate evaluations use applicability metadata; historical evidence remains historical.
plan.compatibility: Applicable JavaScript Change OS changes continue to require node-syntax exactly as before. Non-JavaScript Change OS changes now expose node-syntax as N/A. Other profiles retain current behavior except where the same explicit applicability metadata is intentionally defined.
boundaryCases: Workflow-only Change OS diff requires change-operations-regression and reports node-syntax N/A.
Markdown-only Change OS diff requires change-operations-regression and reports node-syntax N/A.
JavaScript Change OS diff requires both change-operations-regression and node-syntax.
Mixed workflow plus JavaScript Change OS diff requires node-syntax because at least one changed path is applicable.
Omitting node-syntax from an applicable JavaScript Change OS Plan remains FAIL.
Declaring node-syntax when it is not applicable does not convert N/A into PASS or satisfy some other requirement.
testPlan: Verify Risk Check reports explicit N/A for non-JavaScript Change OS node-syntax applicability.
Verify Risk Check still fails when JavaScript Change OS changes omit node-syntax.
Verify mixed Change OS changes require node-syntax.
Open PR and require existing base-owned Change PR Gate and Change Verification Evidence to pass.
Review diff for any weakening of applicable static-check requirements.
Merge to staging only, then reconfirm production/main is unchanged before restarting C3-2 from the new staging main.
plan.promotionRisk: None; staging Change OS contract repair only.
